transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-11
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (PioneerCloud Partnerships), Markus Rehn (PioneerCloud Head of Cloud Products), Sofia Kim (PioneerCloud Technical Lead)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and with me is Ethan, our SE.
[00:10] Lena Ortiz: Hi Maya, Ethan, thanks — excited to chat. Markus and Sofia are here on our end.
[00:18] Markus Rehn: yeah thanks, morning for us.
[00:23] Ethan Cho: quick agenda — intro, Pioneer goals, technical constraints, security, next steps. sound OK?
[00:30] Sofia Kim: yep, good. we'll mostly listen then dive into infra.

[02:05] Maya Patel: To start, curious high level — why partner? what's the target product you imagine with Redwood?
[02:16] Markus Rehn: We're looking to add a managed inference option to our cloud marketplace. Customers keep asking for lower-latency LLM endpoints and turnkey GPU offerings. We want partner options so we don't build everything in-house.
[02:34] Maya Patel: makes sense. are you leaning toward reselling Redwood-hosted API or more like a dedicated co-managed deployment inside Pioneer infra? or both?
[02:43] Lena Ortiz: probably both. the marketplace needs a hosted managed service for SMBs, and for larger enterprise customers they want dedicated single-tenant pools with VPC peering.
[02:56] Ethan Cho: quick clarification — when you say VPC peering, do you mean private peering from Pioneer VPC to Redwood Dedicated, or an on-prem/private deployment we bundle for you?
[03:10] Sofia Kim: ideally both options. for some regulated customers we need private deployments in their VPC; for others, a hosted model is fine.

[04:22] Markus Rehn: timeline-wise, pilot customers start in Q2. we need a partner that can run benchmarks and be production-ready by Q3.
[04:35] Maya Patel: good, realistic. typical win criteria for these pilots? latency SLOs, cost, ease of onboarding?
[04:45] Lena Ortiz: all of the above. also auditability — logs, who accessed what.

[05:12] Ethan Cho: technical questions: what GPU types do you provision today? do you have GPU pools customers can select?
[05:21] Markus Rehn: we've got a mix — A100s, and some 4090-like consumer instances for cost-sensitive customers. we're also piloting H100 with one partner.
[05:34] Ethan Cho: cool. on our side Redwood supports a broad catalog; we can recommend quantized model variants for 4090-class hardware and full precision on A100/H100.

[06:08] Sofia Kim: networking — how does Redwood handle VPC private deployments? we need KMS separation and audit logs.
[06:17] Maya Patel: we offer Redwood Private: customer-managed control plane in a VPC, optional on-prem package. KMS integration for customer keys, and detailed audit logs in the console.
[06:29] Lena Ortiz: is that SOC 2 scoped?
[06:32] Maya Patel: yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II; we'll share the report summary. sometimes the transcribed docs call it SOC2 or S O C two, apologies if the auto-transcript mangles.

[07:10] Markus Rehn: okay good. for the marketplace, commercial margins matter — what's the commercial model for partners? reseller margin, referral, co-sell?
[07:22] Maya Patel: we do a partner program: reseller margins for committed dedicated capacity, referral credits for hosted usage; we can draft examples based on expected utilization.

[08:05] Ethan Cho: technical deep dive question — do you expect model hosting only, or will you want to support model uploads from customers / bring-your-own-model (BYOM)?
[08:15] Sofia Kim: BYOM is important for a few enterprise customers. they want to bring custom models trained in their environment.
[08:22] Ethan Cho: OK, we support pinned model versions and private model uploads in Private deployments; for hosted we have a model catalog and can provide vetted open models.

[09:40] Lena Ortiz: security folks will ask about SSO/SAML. can we do SSO into the console for partner admins and for end-customers?
[09:49] Maya Patel: yes, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC for teams, and audit logs that can be exported.

[11:02] Markus Rehn: curious about performance — do you do automatic batching and KV cache to improve cost?
[11:09] Ethan Cho: yes, the runtime does continuous batching and KV cache; we also have config options to tune batching windows based on latency SLOs. sometimes the transcript says KV "cash" ha, but it's KV cache.

[13:15] Sofia Kim: network egress costs are a concern. if we run Redwood Dedicated in Pioneer region, can we reduce egress?
[13:25] Maya Patel: yes, co-located dedicated pools or private peering reduce egress. we'll outline options and cost tradeoffs.

[14:50] Lena Ortiz: on legal — NDA and standard partner agreement. I'll loop in legal, but do you have a partner MSA?
[14:58] Maya Patel: we have a partner MSA template; we'll send it. expect some negotiation around data residency and warranty clauses for dedicated deployments.

[16:00] Markus Rehn: for the pilot, we want to run a performance benchmark: 1) 13B chat-like model on A100 for latency 2) embedding throughput tests 3) cost per 1M tokens. can Redwood provide benchmarking support?
[16:15] Ethan Cho: absolutely. we can run sample workloads using our Redwood Optimize tooling and share token-level cost breakdowns. ideally we run before/after tests if you can provide representative prompts.

[18:05] Sofia Kim: who will lead the technical deep dive?
[18:09] Maya Patel: Ethan will take the lead and share a test plan.
[18:15] Ethan Cho: I'll coordinate. can Sofia and her infra folks provide topology and network constraints?
[18:21] Sofia Kim: yes. we'll pull together diagrams and a list of test datasets.

[21:30] Lena Ortiz: quick question on support SLAs for marketplace customers vs enterprise — what are the tiers?
[21:36] Maya Patel: hosted has standard SLAs, Dedicated can have SLA-backed latency/uptime targets as part of reserved capacity contracts, and Private gets enterprise support and optional 24/7. we'll attach a support tier sheet.

[24:02] Markus Rehn: any red flags on your side about PioneerCloud working as a channel?
[24:08] Maya Patel: not really; just clarity on ownership for billing and who owns customer success. resale deals need clear attribution but that's solvable.

[26:50] Ethan Cho: operationally, we need to agree on metrics and dashboards — Redwood Console provides per-route/model dashboards and tracing hooks; partner teams can receive role-based access.
[27:00] Sofia Kim: good. what's the expected integration effort for a basic integration?
[27:06] Maya Patel: for a basic hosted integration and marketplace listing, 2-4 weeks of engineering work plus legal onboarding. Dedicated/VPC options add 4-8 weeks depending on network approvals.

[29:20] Lena Ortiz: cost: do you have list pricing for hosted API and a separate pricing for dedicated commits?
[29:27] Maya Patel: yes, hosted API is usage-based; Dedicated is reserved capacity monthly/annual commits. we'll share a pricing sheet with examples.

[31:12] Markus Rehn: on security again, does Redwood support customer-managed keys (KMS) for model encryption?
[31:20] Ethan Cho: yes, KMS integrations supported; keys kept in customer's cloud KMS during Private deployments. hosted has options for customer-managed keys depending on region.

[33:45] Sofia Kim: about monitoring — we need audit logs in our SIEM. can we stream logs?
[33:52] Maya Patel: yes, audit logs export and integrations with common SIEMs. we'll include log schema.

[35:10] Lena Ortiz: any existing partners who've done a similar go-to-market with you?
[35:16] Maya Patel: yes, a few cloud resellers and SI partners. we can provide references after NDA.

[36:30] Markus Rehn: okay, next steps?
[36:34] Maya Patel: quick recap — Redwood will: 1) send partner deck, integration guide, pricing examples and SOC2 summary; 2) Ethan to run technical deep dive and create benchmark test plan; 3) Pioneer to share infra diagrams and sample workloads; 4) legal/NDA follow up from Lena.
[36:50] Lena Ortiz: sounds good. we'll aim to get the infra diagrams by 02-16 and confirm NDA by 02-15.

[38:05] Ethan Cho: I'll send a calendar invite for the deep dive for Feb 18, propose 60-90 min.
[38:12] Maya Patel: and I'll send the partner doc bundle by Friday 02-13.

[39:00] Sofia Kim: quick technical note — when you say "quantized model variants", what quantization levels do you recommend for 4090-class?
[39:10] Ethan Cho: generally 4-bit quantization with f16 fallback for tail cases; we'll include model/quant recommendations in the docs.

[40:30] Markus Rehn: anything else we should cover?
[40:34] Lena Ortiz: no, thanks all.
[40:37] Maya Patel: thanks everyone, appreciate it. we'll follow up with the items discussed.
[40:45] Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: auto-generated, some product names garbled occasionally (e.g., Redwood Dedicate, KV "cash"). This artifact is kept verbatim to preserve conversational context.
